questions.questionText: Which of the following BEST describes machine learning?

options.text: A set of explicit rules programmed by developers to make decisions
A type of AI that enables systems to learn from data and improve without being explicitly programmed
A cloud computing service for running virtual machines
A database system for storing large volumes of data

explanation.correct: Machine learning enables systems to automatically learn patterns from data and improve their performance over time without being explicitly programmed for each scenario.
explanation.incorrect: Rule-based systems = traditional programming. ML learns from data rather than following hand-coded rules.
explanation.examTip: AI > ML > Deep Learning. ML is a subset of AI that learns from data. Deep learning uses neural networks â€” a subset of ML.

metadata.examObjective: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

questions.questionText: What is the difference between supervised and unsupervised learning?

options.text: Supervised learning uses unlabelled data; unsupervised uses labelled data
Supervised learning trains on labelled data with known outputs; unsupervised learning finds patterns in unlabelled data
Supervised learning requires human oversight during inference; unsupervised does not
They are the same â€” both use labelled training data

explanation.correct: Supervised learning uses labelled examples (input + correct output) to learn a mapping function. Unsupervised learning discovers hidden structure in data without labels.
explanation.incorrect: The definitions are reversed in option A. Human oversight is not the distinguishing factor.
explanation.examTip: Supervised = labelled (classification, regression). Unsupervised = unlabelled (clustering, dimensionality reduction). Reinforcement = reward-based.

questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides a fully managed platform for building, training, and deploying machine learning models?

options.text: AWS Lambda
Amazon SageMaker
Amazon EC2
AWS Glue

explanation.correct: Amazon SageMaker is AWS's fully managed ML platform, offering tools for data labelling, feature engineering, model training, hyperparameter tuning, deployment, and monitoring.
explanation.incorrect: Lambda = serverless functions. EC2 = virtual machines. Glue = data integration/ETL.
explanation.examTip: SageMaker is the central AWS ML service. Key features: Studio (IDE), Autopilot (AutoML), JumpStart (pre-built models), Pipelines (MLOps), Clarify (bias/explainability), Canvas (no-code).

questions.questionText: What does Amazon SageMaker Autopilot do?

options.text: Automatically deploys trained models to production endpoints
Automatically builds, trains, and tunes ML models by exploring different algorithms and hyperparameters
Automatically labels training data using active learning
Automatically scales EC2 instances for training jobs

explanation.correct: SageMaker Autopilot is AWS's AutoML solution â€” it automatically explores multiple ML algorithms and hyperparameter combinations, then selects the best model for your dataset.
explanation.incorrect: Auto-deployment = SageMaker endpoints. Data labelling = SageMaker Ground Truth. EC2 scaling = Auto Scaling.
explanation.examTip: Autopilot = AutoML. Provide CSV data, select target column â†’ Autopilot builds, trains, and ranks models automatically. Provides full visibility into the process.

questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides pre-trained ML models for common tasks like image recognition, text analysis, and forecasting without requiring ML expertise?

options.text: Amazon SageMaker
AWS AI Services (Rekognition, Comprehend, Forecast, etc.)
AWS Deep Learning AMIs
Amazon EMR

explanation.correct: AWS AI Services are pre-trained, API-based services that require no ML expertise: Rekognition (vision), Comprehend (NLP), Forecast (time series), Personalize (recommendations), Textract (document), Transcribe (speech), Polly (text-to-speech), Translate.
explanation.incorrect: SageMaker = build custom models. Deep Learning AMIs = developer tools. EMR = big data processing.
explanation.examTip: AWS AI Services: use APIs, no ML knowledge needed. SageMaker: build custom models. The two complement each other.

questions.questionText: What is Amazon Rekognition primarily used for?

options.text: Natural language text analysis
Computer vision tasks like image and video analysis, face detection, and object recognition
Time series forecasting
Converting text to speech

explanation.correct: Amazon Rekognition provides pre-trained computer vision capabilities: object and scene detection, face analysis, face comparison, celebrity recognition, text in images, content moderation, and video analysis.
explanation.incorrect: Text analysis = Comprehend. Forecasting = Forecast. Text-to-speech = Polly.
explanation.examTip: Rekognition use cases: content moderation, face verification, celebrity detection, custom labels (Custom Labels feature), video analysis. No ML expertise needed.

questions.questionText: What does Amazon Comprehend do?

options.text: Converts speech to text
Provides NLP capabilities including sentiment analysis, entity recognition, and language detection
Detects objects in images
Forecasts future values from historical data

explanation.correct: Amazon Comprehend is a natural language processing service that analyses text to extract insights: sentiment, entities (people, places, organisations), key phrases, language detection, syntax, and topic modelling.
explanation.incorrect: Speech to text = Transcribe. Image analysis = Rekognition. Forecasting = Forecast.
explanation.examTip: Comprehend features: Sentiment (positive/negative/neutral/mixed), Entities, Key Phrases, Language, Syntax, Topics. Comprehend Medical for healthcare text.

questions.questionText: Match each AWS AI service to its primary function.

dropdowns.prompt: Converts written text to lifelike speech

explanation.correct: Transcribe = speech-to-text. Polly = text-to-speech. Translate = language translation. Lex = conversational AI/chatbots.
explanation.incorrect: These are distinct AWS AI services each serving a specific use case.
explanation.examTip: AWS AI services map: Rekognition(vision), Comprehend(NLP), Transcribe(speechâ†’text), Polly(textâ†’speech), Translate(translation), Forecast(time series), Personalize(recommendations), Textract(document OCR), Lex(chatbots).

questions.questionText: What is the ML lifecycle and in what order do the steps occur?

options.text: Deploy â†’ Train â†’ Evaluate â†’ Collect Data â†’ Monitor
Collect data â†’ Prepare data â†’ Train model â†’ Evaluate â†’ Deploy â†’ Monitor
Train â†’ Deploy â†’ Collect data â†’ Evaluate â†’ Monitor
Define problem â†’ Deploy â†’ Train â†’ Monitor â†’ Collect data

explanation.correct: The ML lifecycle: 1) Collect and label data, 2) Prepare/engineer features, 3) Train the model, 4) Evaluate performance, 5) Deploy to production, 6) Monitor for drift and retrain as needed.
explanation.incorrect: You cannot train before collecting data. Deployment happens after evaluation, not before.
explanation.examTip: ML lifecycle is circular: monitor â†’ detect drift â†’ retrain â†’ redeploy. SageMaker supports all lifecycle stages in one platform.

questions.questionText: What is Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth used for?

options.text: Monitoring model performance in production
Building high-quality training datasets through human labelling with automated labelling assistance
Running large-scale distributed training jobs
Automatically selecting the best ML algorithm for a dataset

explanation.correct: SageMaker Ground Truth helps build accurate training datasets by combining human annotators (from Amazon Mechanical Turk, private teams, or vendors) with automated labelling to reduce costs.
explanation.incorrect: Monitoring = SageMaker Model Monitor. Distributed training = SageMaker Training Jobs. AutoML = SageMaker Autopilot.
explanation.examTip: Ground Truth = data labelling service. Supports images, text, video. Automated labelling reduces human annotation cost by up to 70%.

questions.scenarioText: A retail company wants to predict daily product demand for the next 30 days using 2 years of historical sales data.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service is BEST suited for this use case?

options.text: Amazon Rekognition
Amazon Forecast
Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Personalize

explanation.correct: Amazon Forecast is a fully managed time series forecasting service that uses ML to generate accurate forecasts from historical data â€” ideal for demand planning, inventory management, and financial forecasting.
explanation.incorrect: Rekognition = vision. Comprehend = text NLP. Personalize = recommendations.
explanation.examTip: Amazon Forecast: time series prediction (demand, revenue, capacity). Uses the same technology as Amazon.com's own demand forecasting. No ML experience required.

questions.questionText: What is Amazon Personalize used for?

options.text: Personalising the AWS Management Console for each user
Building real-time personalised recommendations for users based on their behaviour
Creating personalised training datasets for ML models
Personalising IAM policies based on user roles

explanation.correct: Amazon Personalize provides the same recommendation technology used by Amazon.com â€” enabling developers to build apps with real-time personalised recommendations, personalised search, and user segmentation.
explanation.incorrect: Personalize is for product/content recommendations, not AWS console customisation, training data, or IAM policies.
explanation.examTip: Personalize use cases: product recommendations, content recommendations (Netflix-style), personalised search rankings, next-best action. Uses the same ML as Amazon retail.

questions.questionText: For each statement, indicate whether it correctly describes AWS ML concepts.

statements.text: Amazon Textract can extract structured data from tables and forms in documents.
Amazon Lex is used for building conversational chatbots using voice and text.
SageMaker Canvas requires users to write Python code to build ML models.
Amazon Kendra is an intelligent enterprise search service powered by ML.

explanation.correct: Textract = structured document extraction. Lex = conversational AI (Alexa's technology). Kendra = ML-powered enterprise search. SageMaker Canvas = no-code ML, no Python required.
explanation.incorrect: Canvas is specifically designed for business analysts â€” drag-and-drop ML with no coding needed.
explanation.examTip: SageMaker Canvas = no-code ML for business users. Studio = IDE for data scientists. Autopilot = AutoML. JumpStart = pre-trained models.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of Amazon SageMaker Feature Store?

options.text: A marketplace for purchasing pre-trained ML models
A centralised repository for storing, discovering, and reusing ML features across teams
A storage service for training datasets in S3
A feature flag service for deploying ML models gradually

explanation.correct: SageMaker Feature Store provides a centralised store for ML features â€” enabling teams to define, store, and share features consistently across training and inference, reducing duplicate work.
explanation.incorrect: Pre-trained models = SageMaker JumpStart. Training data = S3. Feature flags = separate DevOps concept.
explanation.examTip: Feature Store: offline store (for training, S3-backed), online store (low-latency inference). Ensures training/serving consistency. Share features across teams.

questions.questionText: What is model drift and how does Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor address it?

options.text: Model drift is when a model becomes too large; Model Monitor compresses it
Model drift is when production data changes and model performance degrades; Model Monitor detects data quality issues, bias, and feature attribution drift
Model drift is when a model moves to a different AWS region; Model Monitor tracks location
Model drift is a training error; Model Monitor prevents it during training

explanation.correct: Model drift occurs when real-world data changes after deployment, causing predictions to degrade. SageMaker Model Monitor continuously monitors endpoints for data quality drift, model quality drift, bias drift, and feature attribution drift.
explanation.incorrect: Model drift is about data distribution changes in production, not model size, region, or training errors.
explanation.examTip: Model Monitor capabilities: Data quality (schema violations), Model quality (accuracy degradation), Bias drift (fairness changes), Feature attribution drift (SHAP value changes). Alerts via CloudWatch.

questions.questionText: What is Amazon Textract primarily used for?

options.text: Translating text between languages
Extracting text, tables, and structured data from scanned documents and images
Analysing the sentiment of customer reviews
Converting text files to audio

explanation.correct: Amazon Textract goes beyond basic OCR â€” it not only extracts text but also identifies document structure (forms, tables, key-value pairs), making it ideal for processing invoices, tax forms, medical records, and contracts.
explanation.incorrect: Translation = Translate. Sentiment = Comprehend. Text-to-audio = Polly.
explanation.examTip: Textract vs Rekognition: Textract = extract text and structured data from documents. Rekognition = detect text in natural images. Textract understands document structure.

questions.questionText: What is Amazon Fraud Detector?

options.text: A network security tool for detecting fraudulent API calls
A fully managed ML service for detecting potentially fraudulent online activity
An IAM policy analyzer for detecting misconfigured permissions
A compliance tool for detecting regulatory violations

explanation.correct: Amazon Fraud Detector uses ML to detect fraud in real time â€” account takeover, fake account creation, online payment fraud, transaction fraud â€” using the same technology AWS uses internally.
explanation.incorrect: Fraud Detector is specifically for detecting fraudulent business activities, not API security, IAM analysis, or compliance.
explanation.examTip: Fraud Detector use cases: online payment fraud, fake account creation, promo/loyalty abuse, account takeover. No ML experience needed â€” uses your historical fraud data.

questions.questionText: What type of ML problem is spam email classification?

options.text: Regression
Binary classification
Clustering
Anomaly detection

explanation.correct: Spam classification is binary classification â€” predict one of two categories (spam or not spam) for each email based on its features.
explanation.incorrect: Regression predicts continuous numbers. Clustering groups without labels. Anomaly detection finds outliers. Spam has two fixed classes = binary classification.
explanation.examTip: Classification types: Binary (2 classes: spam/not, fraud/legit), Multi-class (3+ classes: dog/cat/bird), Multi-label (multiple labels per item). All use labelled training data.

questions.scenarioText: A company has an ML model that achieves 92% accuracy on training data but only 64% on test data.
questions.questionText: What does this indicate and what should the team do?

options.text: The model is underfitting â€” increase training time
The model is overfitting â€” apply regularisation, get more data, or simplify the model
The model is performing well â€” 64% test accuracy is acceptable
The test data is wrong â€” discard it and use more training data

explanation.correct: High training accuracy (92%) with low test accuracy (64%) is overfitting â€” the model memorised training data rather than learning generalisable patterns. Solutions: regularisation (L1/L2), more training data, simpler model, dropout.
explanation.incorrect: Underfitting shows low accuracy on both sets. 64% test with 92% train is clearly overfitting. Test data should not be discarded.
explanation.examTip: SageMaker tools for overfitting: Autopilot tests multiple algorithms with regularisation, Debugger monitors training metrics. Use cross-validation to detect early.

questions.questionText: What is Amazon SageMaker Canvas?

options.text: A data visualisation tool for creating charts from ML model outputs
A no-code ML tool enabling business analysts to build ML models without programming
A drawing tool for creating ML pipeline architecture diagrams
An interface for managing SageMaker training job logs

explanation.correct: SageMaker Canvas is a visual, no-code ML tool designed for business analysts â€” import data, build models with point-and-click, generate predictions, and share models with data science teams without writing any code.
explanation.incorrect: Canvas is specifically no-code ML for non-technical users, not a visualisation, diagram, or logging tool.
explanation.examTip: Canvas target user: business analysts. Studio target user: data scientists. Autopilot target user: MLOps/data scientists wanting AutoML. Canvas outputs can be imported into Studio.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of Amazon SageMaker Pipelines?

options.text: Network data pipelines for transferring ML training data
A CI/CD service for ML that automates and manages end-to-end ML workflows
Data transformation pipelines using Apache Spark
An API gateway for routing requests to different ML endpoints

explanation.correct: SageMaker Pipelines is a purpose-built CI/CD service for ML â€” defining, automating, and managing repeatable ML workflows (data prep â†’ training â†’ evaluation â†’ deployment) with step tracking and reuse.
explanation.incorrect: Pipelines is for ML workflow automation, not network data transfer, Spark processing, or API routing.
explanation.examTip: SageMaker Pipelines = MLOps. Define DAG of steps (Processing, Training, Evaluation, Condition, Model Register, Transform). Automate retraining when new data arrives.

questions.questionText: What is Amazon Comprehend Medical?

options.text: A health insurance benefit for Amazon employees
A version of Amazon Comprehend specialised for extracting medical information from clinical notes and medical records
A medical imaging analysis service
A HIPAA compliance certification for AWS services

explanation.correct: Amazon Comprehend Medical uses NLP to extract medical entities from unstructured text â€” medical conditions, medications, dosages, test results, anatomy, and protected health information (PHI).
explanation.incorrect: Comprehend Medical is an NLP service for clinical text, not an employee benefit, imaging service, or compliance certification.
explanation.examTip: Comprehend Medical capabilities: extract PHI, medications, conditions, anatomy, test results from clinical notes. HIPAA eligible. Extract ICD-10-CM and RxNorm codes.

questions.questionText: What is deep learning?

options.text: A type of machine learning that uses deep databases for training
A subset of machine learning using artificial neural networks with many layers to learn complex representations from data
Machine learning models that require deep domain expertise to build
A technique for deeply analysing structured data in relational databases

explanation.correct: Deep learning uses neural networks with multiple hidden layers â€” 'deep' refers to the depth of layers. These layers automatically learn increasingly abstract representations of data, enabling tasks like image recognition and natural language understanding.
explanation.incorrect: Deep learning refers to neural network depth, not database depth, domain expertise, or database analytics.
explanation.examTip: Deep learning excels at: image recognition (CNNs), NLP/LLMs (Transformers), speech recognition (RNNs). Requires large datasets and significant compute (GPUs/TPUs).

questions.questionText: What is the difference between batch inference and real-time inference in Amazon SageMaker?

options.text: Batch inference is faster than real-time inference
Batch Transform processes large datasets offline; real-time endpoints respond to individual requests immediately
Real-time inference only works with tabular data
They are the same but run in different AWS regions

explanation.correct: SageMaker Batch Transform processes entire datasets in bulk (e.g., score all customers overnight). Real-time inference endpoints respond immediately to individual requests (e.g., fraud check during payment processing).
explanation.incorrect: Real-time is faster per request. Both support various data types. They serve fundamentally different use cases.
explanation.examTip: SageMaker inference types: Real-time endpoint (immediate, persistent), Serverless endpoint (on-demand, auto-scale to zero), Batch Transform (offline bulk scoring), Async endpoint (large payloads).

questions.questionText: What is Amazon SageMaker Studio?

options.text: A mobile app for monitoring SageMaker training jobs
A fully integrated web-based IDE for the complete ML lifecycle in a single environment
A recording studio for creating AI-generated audio content
A visual analytics dashboard for ML model metrics

explanation.correct: SageMaker Studio is a unified web-based IDE providing all tools for the ML lifecycle in one place: notebooks, data preparation, feature engineering, model training, debugging, deployment, and monitoring.
explanation.incorrect: Studio is a web IDE for data scientists, not a mobile app, audio tool, or dashboard.
explanation.examTip: SageMaker Studio components: JupyterLab notebooks, Data Wrangler, Feature Store, Experiments, Debugger, Pipelines, Model Registry, Monitor. All in one browser-based IDE.

questions.questionText: What is transfer learning and how does it relate to foundation models?

options.text: Moving a trained ML model between AWS regions
Using knowledge learned during training on one task to improve performance on a different but related task
Transferring training data between S3 buckets
Converting a model from one framework to another

explanation.correct: Transfer learning takes a model trained on a large general task and adapts it for a specific use case. Foundation models embody transfer learning at scale â€” pre-trained on massive data, then fine-tuned or prompted for specific tasks.
explanation.incorrect: Transfer learning is a machine learning technique, not region migration, data transfer, or framework conversion.
explanation.examTip: Foundation models = transfer learning at massive scale. The pre-training on diverse data transfers knowledge that benefits many downstream applications through prompting or fine-tuning.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of Amazon SageMaker Experiments?

options.text: A/B testing for ML models in production
Tracking, comparing, and managing multiple ML training runs to identify the best model
Experimenting with Bedrock foundation models in the playground
Testing new AWS AI service features before general availability

explanation.correct: SageMaker Experiments tracks training runs (hyperparameters, metrics, artifacts) and lets you compare multiple experiments to identify which model configuration performed best â€” enabling systematic model development.
explanation.incorrect: Production A/B testing = SageMaker endpoints with traffic splitting. Bedrock playground is separate. Feature testing = AWS previews.
explanation.examTip: SageMaker Experiments: log runs â†’ compare metrics (accuracy, loss) â†’ visualise â†’ select best run â†’ register winning model. Integrates with Studio for visual comparison.

questions.questionText: What AWS service is used for building conversational AI interfaces (chatbots) using voice and text?

options.text: Amazon Polly
Amazon Lex
Amazon Transcribe
Amazon Comprehend

explanation.correct: Amazon Lex is the same technology powering Alexa â€” enabling developers to build conversational interfaces using voice and text with natural language understanding (NLU) and automatic speech recognition (ASR).
explanation.incorrect: Polly = text to speech. Transcribe = speech to text. Comprehend = text NLP. Lex = conversational interface/chatbots.
explanation.examTip: Lex + Lambda = conversational AI with business logic. Lex + Kendra = intelligent Q&A chatbot. Lex + Bedrock = generative AI-powered conversation.

questions.questionText: What is reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF)?

options.text: A technique for having humans manually review and fix ML errors
A training technique that uses human preference feedback to align LLM outputs with human values and expectations
A way for humans to provide real-time feedback during model inference
Reinforcement learning where humans serve as the environment

explanation.correct: RLHF fine-tunes LLMs by having humans compare model outputs and indicate preferences. A reward model is trained on these preferences, then used to guide further training â€” making the model more helpful, harmless, and honest.
explanation.incorrect: RLHF is a specific training alignment technique, not manual error correction, real-time feedback, or humans-as-environment.
explanation.examTip: RLHF is used to align LLMs: ChatGPT, Claude, and other major LLMs use RLHF. The reward model learns human preferences and guides the LLM toward better responses.

questions.questionText: Match each ML evaluation metric to what it measures.

dropdowns.prompt: Percentage of correct predictions out of all predictions
Percentage of actual positives correctly identified (minimise false negatives)
Harmonic mean of precision and recall

explanation.correct: Accuracy = correct/total. Recall = true positives/(true positives + false negatives). F1 = harmonic mean of precision and recall (balances both).
explanation.incorrect: These are the four primary classification metrics. Each reveals different aspects of model performance.
explanation.examTip: Metric selection: Imbalanced data â†’ F1 or AUC-ROC over accuracy. Medical/fraud (miss = costly) â†’ maximise Recall. Spam filter (false positives = annoying) â†’ maximise Precision.

questions.questionText: What is Amazon SageMaker Model Registry used for?

options.text: A marketplace for buying and selling ML models
A centralised repository for versioning, tracking, and managing the lifecycle of ML models from development to production
A registry of AWS compliance certifications for ML services
A domain registry for AI-related domain names

explanation.correct: SageMaker Model Registry stores trained model versions with metadata (metrics, training data, parameters), manages approval workflows (pending/approved/rejected), and tracks lineage from training run to deployment.
explanation.incorrect: Model Registry is for internal model governance, not a marketplace, compliance registry, or domain names.
explanation.examTip: Model Registry workflow: train â†’ evaluate â†’ register model â†’ approval workflow â†’ deploy to endpoint. Tracks: version, metrics, training job, approval status, deployment history.
